name: q063
question:
What is the volume, composition, and significance of the deep biosphere?
The deep-ocean biosphere is an extreme environment, consisting of bacteria and archaea living in depths greater than 1,000 meters (3,280 feet), in the absence of light, in temperatures of only 4°C (39°F), and in pressures about 40 to 110 times that of Earth’s atmosphere. Our increased understanding of the deep ocean is shedding new light on climate change, biodiversity, natural resources, and even our search for extraterrestrial life.
